record.file_problem: Not garbled or cut off; this is repository metadata, README, and file list only. Code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal and held-out-loss outcomes after a weight-edit removal of a harmful-minus-harmless activation direction. This tests the practical removal effect, but it does not report the original all-layers-and-positions activation ablation or an addition intervention.
record.gate_note: The README reports Stage 4 abliteration outcomes. Candidate-layer scores are described as being used to select layer 23, so those selection values are not rows. DPO training results are omitted because they report training effects, not a test of the direction. Other tokenizer and pretraining results do not bear on the claim.
record.test_reason: The repo applies Arditi-style weight orthogonalization to its own DPO-aligned 135M Vietnamese model. It reports strict refusal rates before and after, plus held-out loss. That is the original removal recipe in a new setting (language, scale, alignment pipeline), with results bearing on V1's ablation part and on V2. The direction is taken from layer 23 but projected out of every residual-writing matrix, which matches the original's all-layer weight edit.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The README reports that weight orthogonalization with the layer-23 direction (projected out of all residual-writing matrices) cuts strict refusal on harmful sets from 69–94% to 5–28%, with held-out loss +0.02. Command prompts keep the most refusals, and some unrefused answers are off-topic, which the author attributes to the weak 135M base.
record.recipe_differences: This is a repository/tool pipeline, not a stated replication. It computes a harmful-minus-harmless direction from the final prompt token, selects a candidate layer using refusal rate and held-out loss, then orthogonalizes weights at that layer. It does not report the original activation ablation at every layer and position or an addition test.
record.method_sensitivity: Prompt form changes the reported outcome: harmful command prompts retain a 28% refusal rate after editing, compared with 12% for long prompts and 5% for short prompts.
record.problems: README-reported results only; code and result artifacts were not read or run. The reported refusal evaluation uses a strict regex detector, and the harmful prompt sets have 100 prompts each. The capability-related check is held-out loss only. The README says some responses after abliteration are off-topic rather than compliant.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible Stage 4 outcome rows were omitted. Layer-candidate values used for selection are excluded, as are DPO training results and unrelated tokenizer/pretraining results.

record.verdict_notes: This is a hobby repo README with no uncertainty reported and n=100 per set. The refusal detector is a strict regex (apologies / 'cannot help'), which may undercount refusals and inflate removal. The record's wording that the edit is 'at layer 23' should be corrected: only the direction comes from layer 23. The 'Evaluation Matrix' table (perplexity 'Same as Stage 3') looks like planned targets, not measurements, so it was not used.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test activation projection at every layer and position, addition of the direction, or broad general capability beyond held-out loss. The reported intervention is a weight edit at selected layer 23.
Tests one 135M Vietnamese model and one selected layer; no other released models or weight-edit variants are reported.
No jailbreak suppression or adversarial training against ablation is tested.
No comparison of one direction with an affine subspace, cone, or multiple directions is reported.
No separate harmfulness judgment and refusal-decision representations are measured.
The direction is computed for Vietnamese prompts; transfer of a direction across languages, variants, or base-to-instruct models is not tested.
The README gives refusal rates for DPO runs, but does not test whether different training choices change the existence of a removable direction.
